plans.note: No limitation-of-liability heading appears in the supplied outline; numbering gaps (sections 3, 4, 6, 9, 11) mean a cap may sit in an unlisted section. Check sec-12 (Indemnity), where damages limits are often bundled, before concluding it is missing.

Sec-12 is the operative indemnity. Test whether TrueLink indemnifies Client for third-party IP infringement in the licensed platform and hosting services, and whether Client's reciprocal indemnity (likely tied to sec-8 client covenants and sec-7 e-mail conduct) is kept narrow and capped.
No non-compete heading is visible. Any restraint on the businesses Client may operate would most plausibly appear as a client covenant in sec-8 or as a use restriction in the sec-2 licence grant.

Watch for sole-source or 'sole provider of hosting/licensed services' language in the sec-2 licence grant or the sec-8 client covenants; a volume-linked exclusivity could also hide in sec-5 compensation.
Pricing lives in sec-5. Only flag if Client is obliged to extend TrueLink its best terms; an MFN running in Client's favour is welcome and should not be redlined.

No standalone non-solicit heading; such covenants are often appended to client covenants (sec-8) or to the confidentiality section (sec-10). Accept narrow, time-limited terms with a general-advertising carve-out.

No term/termination heading appears in the supplied outline; it may reside in an unlisted numbered section (3, 4, 6, 9 or 11). Confirm whether Client has notice-based exit without penalty and whether TrueLink can terminate mid-term.

Term and renewal mechanics are not in the visible outline; any renewal price uplift would tie back to sec-5 compensation. Check the unlisted sections for auto-renewal and the non-renewal notice window.

No general/miscellaneous or governing law heading is supplied; likely in an unlisted trailing section. Confirm the forum is New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales and that disputes go to courts rather than foreign arbitration.
No assignment or miscellaneous section in the outline. Verify Client may assign to affiliates and successors and that TrueLink has no termination right on Client's change of control.

Ownership will turn on the sec-2 licence grant read with the sec-1 definitions (Hosting Services, and any site/content/data definitions). Confirm Client retains ownership of its site content, customer/borrower data and any paid-for deliverables, with no assignment or licence-back of Client IP to TrueLink; sec-10 may carry data-confidentiality support.

Sec-2 is the grant. Check scope for affiliate and contractor use, territory, and whether the licence is revocable at will or terminable only for cause; sec-1 definitions may narrow the licensed subject matter.

No audit heading is visible; a usage or records audit right would most likely be attached to the sec-8 client covenants or to sec-5 fee verification. If present, test notice, frequency, off-site review and who bears cost.

Look for per-incident penalties or fixed damages payable by Client in sec-7 (unsolicited commercial e-mail, a common home for stipulated penalties) and in sec-5 (late fees, early-termination charges). Service credits running to Client are welcome and not flagged.

Sec-8 covers only Client's warranties; a TrueLink performance/hosting warranty and any disclaimer may sit in an unlisted section. Confirm a meaningful warranty period and a real remedy (re-performance or refund) for the Hosting Services.

No insurance heading in the outline. As TrueLink hosts Client's site and handles Client data, expect commercial general liability, professional/tech E&O and cyber cover; if absent anywhere, treat as missing.
Sec-5 compensation is the only plausible home for minimum fees, guaranteed volumes or take-or-pay. Flag only if a commitment exists without a corresponding exit right.

No termination-effects section is visible; sec-10 may require return or destruction of confidential information, which is not a substitute for site/data migration assistance and return of Client data in a usable format.
